storm_from_model.speaker: narrator
storm_from_model.text: Fourteen days after the ridge commission closed, Yue was still at the receiving workshop. Her three study mornings had become finished notes, and the corrected model lay under its linen cover. A notice arrived describing the last storm as an unforeseeable failure of warning. Jiang read it twice. The workshop had sent its warning before the rain. Somewhere between that message and the village bell, somebody's account had changed.

storm_from_route.speaker: narrator
storm_from_route.text: Fourteen days after the ridge commission closed, Yue returned to the receiving workshop carrying her ordinary cart notes. Her paid practice had ended safely; the upper spur remained shut. The keeper gave her a notice about storm compensation, then asked why the notice said the road's warning had arrived too late. Yue remembered the courier passing while they replaced the wheel peg. Memory alone could not settle the hour. Jiang invited her to examine what had survived.

storm_from_home.speaker: narrator
storm_from_home.text: Fourteen days after the ridge commission closed, Yue came back from the west kiln at Jiang's invitation. Her mother's cracked flour jar had survived the storm, but a neighbor's roof had not. The compensation notice called their losses the consequence of an unforeseeable warning failure. Yue carried the invitation and a copied receipt her mother had kept beneath the flour shelf. Its date differed from the date printed in the village account.

storm_arrival_001.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_001.text: The receiving workshop smelled of wet wool and polished brass. Jiang stood beside a small handbell whose clapper had been wrapped in cord. Beyond the window, the repaired lower road carried a single empty cart. The upper spur was still closed. Yue put her bag down and asked whether this was another formation test. Jiang shook her head. 'The rod report concerns the road. This concerns what people were told, and where the repair money went.'

storm_arrival_002.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_002.text: The storm had damaged eleven roofs, two grain sheds and the bridge's outer rail. Nobody had died, but a carter's broken ankle would keep him from the harvest run. The council's relief chest held one hundred eighty copper at opening. Its published ledger now showed one hundred forty paid out. Four families standing outside the workshop held receipts for smaller amounts than the names beside their doors had supposedly received.

storm_arrival_003.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_003.text: Jiang's copy of the warning named an uncertain interval of dangerous weather, not a promised hour of lightning. A road keeper had carried that message to the village on the previous afternoon. The council's account described it arriving after midnight. Both statements could be wrong in different ways. Yue wanted a clean contradiction, like two lines failing to meet. Jiang handed her three envelopes instead. Each contained one person's incomplete attempt to remember a frightening night.

storm_arrival_004.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_004.text: The council steward arrived with an inkstone and a bruised pear. He offered the pear to Yue, then recognized that it looked like a gift at the wrong time and set it aside. 'I signed the account,' he said. 'I did not write every entry.' Jiang asked for the original book. He agreed to bring it to the archive the next morning. His willingness made the book obtainable. It did not make his account reliable.

storm_arrival_005.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_005.text: Yue's new task was twelve days of ordinary copying, interviews and supervised apparatus comparison. Jiang had arranged meals and eighteen copper from the independent road fund, recorded separately from the contested relief chest. Shen Qing would join for four archive afternoons after his Azure Cloud duties. A village clerk would retain the originals. Yue could inspect a numbered copy without becoming the custodian of somebody else's last proof of a lost roof.

storm_arrival_006.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_006.text: At Azure Cloud, Elder Yun listened to the outline before lending a dry reference register. Its entries described bell tests and messenger handovers from two earlier seasons. She could compare dates; she could not see a vanished night through the seal. 'If you find a contradiction, preserve both sides,' she said. Yue noticed a white repair stitch in Yun's sleeve. The elder's authority looked smaller when it had to work through paper, and more useful.

storm_arrival_007.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_007.text: Shen Qing met Yue at the archive stairs carrying a lunch packet with one corner already eaten. He admitted he had expected a dramatic storm investigation. The archive smelled of mice rather than thunder. Yue laughed, then looked at the ledger on the table and stopped. There was something embarrassing in wanting damaged lives to provide a satisfying adventure. Shen put the food between them. 'We can be disappointed in the scenery and still do the work.'

storm_arrival_008.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_008.text: The village clerk had numbered the ledger's leaves in brown ink before any of them arrived. The relief entries were black; a later reconciliation line was blue. One leaf had a nick near the sewing hole. The clerk placed a clear sheet over it so Yue could mark the nick's location without rubbing the paper. A pasted receipt covered half a surname. They would need its counterpart before deciding whose name the obscured strokes represented.

storm_arrival_009.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_009.text: The first receipt belonged to a widow who sold roof reeds. Its stamped amount was twelve copper. Her ledger entry said twenty. She remembered receiving ten after a two-copper fee, though the council notice listed no fee. Yue copied all three numbers instead of replacing them with one attractive total. A dishonest ledger and a permitted deduction could coexist. Their next question would have to determine which deductions had actually been authorized.

storm_arrival_010.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_010.text: The steward said eight copper had bought replacement rope for the bell tower, charged against the widow's grant by mistake. Jiang asked where the rope was fitted. 'The tower,' he answered, too quickly. The bell keeper had replaced no rope that week. That disagreement made the expense worth following. It did not yet tell them whether the steward had invented the purchase or remembered a legitimate delivery at the wrong place.

storm_arrival_011.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_011.text: On the table, Yue drew three columns: message movement, bell condition and copper movement. Shen wanted to join them with arrows immediately. She kept the columns separate. A silent bell could explain why people stayed in their houses; a padded expense could explain where relief money went. The same person might be responsible for both, or the storm might have exposed unrelated failures. Their report would become weaker if its first sketch insisted on one villain.

storm_arrival_012.speaker: narrator
storm_arrival_012.text: Jiang offered three starting points. The receiving book could establish what the messenger delivered. The ordinary lower route could test whether a afternoon arrival was plausible. Households could show what warning they actually heard and what money reached them. Every line would require later comparison. Yue chose where to begin, knowing the others would collect the remaining copies while she was away. Choosing a first question would shape her attention without erasing the other evidence.

storm_inquiry_choice.speaker: narrator
storm_inquiry_choice.text: Rain tapped against the archive shutters while the first day's light thinned. Yue could begin with paper, the messenger's ordinary route, or the households whose accounts had become numbers in the council book. Jiang would preserve the untouched originals and ask the clerk to copy the other two sets. None of these starting points could determine intent alone. They needed a question specific enough to carry into the next morning.

choices.text: Compare the receiving book with the warning copy.
Walk the lower message route with its keeper.
Hear the households before interpreting their receipts.

storm_paper_001.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_001.text: The receiving book had been kept beside a kitchen hearth rather than the bell tower. Its first pages smelled of onions. Yue disliked the disorder until the clerk pointed out the old flour tally on the same afternoon's leaf. The miller's duplicate fixed that delivery before dusk. The warning entry followed it and preceded the evening lamp issue. Those independent transactions bounded an interval. They did not produce a minute the book had never recorded.

storm_paper_002.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_002.text: Shen copied the warning's broken corner, including a fragment that looked like the beginning of a second signature. Yue almost asked the steward to identify it. Instead they checked the road keeper's retained half. The fragment joined a fold mark, not another name. A torn corner could resemble a guilty stroke when somebody expected guilt. Yue wrote the mistaken first reading in her working notes so she would remember how easily certainty had arrived.

storm_paper_003.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_003.text: The warning mentioned the lower bridge, eleven exposed roofs and a likely need for early grain shelter. It did not require reopening the upper road. The council's later summary substituted 'all ridge routes' for 'lower crossing.' Jiang traced the change through three copies. The first summary was accurate; the second had the broad phrase. The third copied that phrase exactly. The error had a location in the copying sequence, even before it had an explanation.

storm_paper_004.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_004.text: The second summary was signed by a temporary scribe. She had gone inland for her brother's wedding and could not answer that week. The steward asked them to call the mistake hers in the interim. Yue refused to convert absence into admission. They could state where the phrase first appeared and request her dated explanation. Blame would have to wait. Shen gave the steward a copy of the proposed wording and watched him read it slowly.

storm_paper_005.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_005.text: The kitchen register's warning line carried an arrival mark shaped like a hooked reed. The road keeper used a square mark on his own book. Yue feared a substituted entry until the clerk explained that the kitchen attendant marked receiving, while the keeper marked handing over. Two different marks were expected. They tested the explanation against five older deliveries. In each case the pair differed in the same way. This difference was ordinary administration, not a discovered fraud.

storm_paper_006.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_006.text: Under the pasted widow's receipt, the surname ended with two short strokes. The ledger's index named a different household whose roof had remained intact. The clerk found the original transfer slip in a bundle labeled 'tower expense.' Its number matched the widow's receipt. A misplaced slip and a mistaken name could explain part of the discrepancy. The excess amount still required a destination, and the book's neat total could not supply one.

storm_paper_007.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_007.text: The lamp-oil seller brought her own afternoon account. She had supplied two bowls before the warning arrived and a third after the council met. Her prices matched her earlier week. Yue copied the entries but did not call the seller independent of the council until asking who owed her money. Half her payment remained outstanding. Dependence did not make her account false. It told the reviewers which pressure she might face for contradicting a powerful customer.

storm_paper_008.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_008.text: Shen suggested detecting later writing by holding the page against a hot lamp. The clerk stopped his hand before the book moved. Heat could damage the ink and the paper beneath it. They used reflected daylight and a clean mirror instead, recording visible differences without claiming their ages. When the nicked leaf lifted, Yue saw a grain of blue grit near the binding. It matched the inkstone on the steward's table but proved no writing date.

storm_paper_009.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_009.text: At the end of the afternoon, the book established that a warning was entered before the final lamp issue and that the broad route phrase arose during summary copying. The duplicate receipt connected one household's payment to an expense bundle. None established why the bell was silent. Yue felt their progress as a narrowing corridor rather than an opening vista. Jiang said a corridor still took them somewhere if they stopped drawing doors it did not contain.

storm_paper_010.speaker: narrator
storm_paper_010.text: Yue carried the clerk's certified copy to the workshop, leaving the original beneath its weighted cloth. Shen stayed to finish the index. Outside, children were throwing pear seeds at the archive wall, pretending the marks were storm stars. One asked whether Yue had found the liar. She answered that she had found two sentences that could not both describe the same handover. The child looked disappointed. Yue understood the appetite behind that disappointment.

storm_route_001.speaker: narrator
storm_route_001.text: The lower route began with eighteen shallow steps and a turn past the drying shed. The keeper walked at the pace he had used with a message box, carrying an equal ordinary load. Yue started an hourglass at the workshop. They did not pretend that today's clear path reproduced the storm day's muddy one. A timed walk could challenge an impossible arrival claim. It could not reconstruct each pause, greeting or stumble of the storm afternoon.

storm_route_002.speaker: narrator
storm_route_002.text: The keeper stopped where a pear cart had blocked the corner on the original journey. Its owner remembered moving before the second lamp issue. She had a delivery tally, but no clock. Yue sketched the cart's length and the passage left beside it. Shen wanted to call the obstruction decisive. An adult could have squeezed past carrying the message box. The cart explained a delay measured in steps, not the missing evening the published account required.

storm_route_003.speaker: narrator
storm_route_003.text: At the kitchen door, the keeper showed the bench on which he had set the warning box. The attendant remembered its copper hinge striking the wood. An old dent lay near her finger. Yue measured the hinge beside it and found it too narrow. The dent came from another box. The attendant looked ashamed, though her memory of receiving the warning might still be sound. Yue crossed out the dent claim and kept the rest attributed to its speaker.

storm_route_004.speaker: narrator
storm_route_004.text: They walked to the bell tower on the checked village paving. The keeper had not gone there that afternoon; his duty ended at the kitchen handover. Yue had assumed a messenger would naturally continue to the bell. The attendant corrected her. The council assigned a separate runner after reading any warning. Responsibility passed through another pair of feet. A late sound at the tower could coexist with an early delivery to the council.

storm_route_005.speaker: narrator
storm_route_005.text: The runner's roster listed a fifteen-year-old apprentice who had been helping the baker. His flour mark appeared on the evening tray sheet. He said he carried a message to the tower after that tray left the oven. Yue asked him to show the path with an empty box. At the tower's lower landing, he halted. The keeper had turned him back because the stair rail was loose. He had returned the box to the kitchen.

storm_route_006.speaker: narrator
storm_route_006.text: The loose rail had been repaired the next morning. The carpenter's invoice named ordinary nails, one brace and a half-day of labor. A blackened scorch above it belonged to an older strike, visible in last season's sketch. Yue kept the two marks apart. Shen crouched beside the brace and tested its current movement. It held. Today's sound rail did not disprove yesterday's refusal, any more than the old scorch proved this storm's damage.

storm_route_007.speaker: narrator
storm_route_007.text: The bell keeper described his refusal as a tower closure, not a refusal to warn. He had expected the runner to use the handbell stored in the kitchen. The kitchen attendant had expected the keeper to ring from below using the spare line. Neither had named that assumption aloud. Yue felt anger drain from the explanation and then return differently. A gap nobody intended could still leave households under a collapsing roof.

storm_route_008.speaker: narrator
storm_route_008.text: The spare line was coiled in a cupboard with a tag that said 'wet test pending.' Its leather eye had split during the last rain. No replacement line hung beside it. The expense ledger nevertheless showed payment for a fitted warning rope three days before the storm. Yue copied the tag, its old inspection number and the empty hook. They had found an absent object that the book treated as installed, and a maintenance problem people had worked around in silence.

storm_route_009.speaker: narrator
storm_route_009.text: Before returning, Yue and the keeper practiced the alternate route to the high granary yard. The ordinary gate latch stuck under the weight of swollen wood. A child could open it only if an adult lifted the bar first. The keeper wrote a repair request, separate from the investigation. The yard was the village's refuge in another storm. Waiting for a fraud finding to fix its gate would mistake explanation for protection.

storm_route_010.speaker: narrator
storm_route_010.text: The second hourglass emptied after they reached the workshop. The walk and stops made the published after-midnight delivery implausible, but could not establish the actual hour. Yue handed Jiang the roster copy, the split spare-line sketch and the granary gate request. Her boots were muddy and her shoulders tired. She had used no qi on the path. The most valuable thing she brought back was another handover they had not known to ask about.

storm_households_001.speaker: narrator
storm_households_001.text: The first household had spread its remaining roof reeds on a dry floor. Yue sat beside them while the widow counted the twelve-copper receipt and the ten copper she received. She did not count the two missing coins as a mystery; the runner had called them a tower levy. The mystery was why the public ledger said twenty. Her daughter asked whether refusing a new interview would lose the grant. Yue showed her the council's written answer before opening her notebook.

storm_households_002.speaker: narrator
storm_households_002.text: At the next house, a potter remembered three bell sounds before rain and four after. Her husband insisted there had been none. They argued until Yue asked what each had been doing. The potter had worked beside her kiln's metal cooling tray; he had been asleep behind the wall. She demonstrated its ringing edge with an ordinary spoon. The sound resembled a small bell. That resemblance could explain their disagreement without making either memory a lie.

storm_households_003.speaker: narrator
storm_households_003.text: An injured carter lay with his ankle supported on folded blankets. He had heard a shout about the bridge but thought it concerned a stray ox. His receipt named sixteen copper. He received sixteen, and his entry showed sixteen. Yue recorded the agreement with the same care as the discrepancies. If only the troubled households appeared in the report, reviewers might conclude that every payment had failed. The accurately paid grant would also help trace the book's genuine receipt style.

storm_households_004.speaker: narrator
storm_households_004.text: The carter resented the keeper for barring the upper road. He had tried to take that shortcut after the warning and fallen on the lower turn while arguing with another driver. The closed spur had not caused his fracture directly. Neither had his anger erased his need for treatment. Yue wrote the ordinary circumstances and left the injury grant unchanged. Jiang had warned her that correcting a causal claim must not become a way of punishing an unpleasant witness.

storm_households_005.speaker: narrator
storm_households_005.text: In the grain shed, six families kept sacks under a shared cover. The cover had been bought with their own pooled copper after the storm. Its seller's receipt showed an amount later claimed as a council relief purchase. The same cloth could appear in two accounts legitimately if the council reimbursed them. No household had received reimbursement. Yue asked the seller for his duplicate rather than accusing the runner standing beside the sacks.

storm_households_006.speaker: narrator
storm_households_006.text: The runner said he collected receipts wherever he found repair work, believing the steward needed proof of village losses. Nobody told him to mark privately funded purchases as council expenditure. He had copied the cover's amount correctly. Yue asked him to show the instruction note. It requested 'evidence of completed repairs' without asking who paid. A careless instruction had supplied raw material for a misleading account. They still needed to identify who converted the evidence into a payment claim.

storm_households_007.speaker: narrator
storm_households_007.text: Two brothers had borrowed a handbell from the kitchen during the storm. It made only a dry click. They remembered cord wrapped around its clapper but disagreed about when it was removed. Yue found the same cord still stored in the box. Its fibers had tightened beneath old dust. That condition supported prolonged storage in a muffled state; it did not reveal who last touched it. A winter procession might explain the wrapping better than deliberate sabotage.

storm_households_008.speaker: narrator
storm_households_008.text: The kitchen attendant recalled muffling the handbell during the winter naming vigil, when a baby slept beside the stove. She forgot to remove the cord afterward. The bell keeper had never checked that substitute before declaring the tower closed. Yue wanted to assign the whole failure to the forgotten cord. The warning had also needed a runner, an instruction and a refuge gate that opened. One recoverable mistake would make an attractive ending and an incomplete account.

storm_households_009.speaker: narrator
storm_households_009.text: Mo Ran came through the village carrying medicinal roots for the carter. He had seen enough accusations to distrust a tidy one. 'A missing coin is not always a thief,' he told Yue, 'but a thousand explanations can hide one just as well.' He helped lift the refuge gate bar while the carpenter planed its swollen edge. The warning problem received a small repair before the payment problem received a verdict.

storm_households_010.speaker: narrator
storm_households_010.text: At dusk, Yue totaled the copied receipts and left the uncertain memories in a separate envelope. Three payments agreed with the ledger; four showed differences; two expenses had apparently paid for privately purchased repairs. Jiang would reconcile the numbers against the originals. The widow sent a bundle of dry reeds for the workshop stove and asked to have her own name spelled correctly in the report. Yue wrote it again, checking every stroke with her.

storm_compare_001.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_001.text: By the fourth morning, the clerk had gathered all three sets of evidence. The warning had reached the kitchen before the final evening lamp issue. The tower runner had been turned back at its loose rail. The spare line was unfit, the substitute handbell muffled, and the granary gate difficult to open. Each discovery described a different link. Yue arranged them along the floor on separate cards, leaving gaps where an assumption had passed for a handover.

storm_compare_002.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_002.text: The payment copies gave a firmer total. One hundred two copper had actually reached households and ordinary repair sellers. The ledger's published one hundred forty treated another thirty-eight as household benefit. Its supporting slips assigned that same thirty-eight to rope, cover cloth and grain shelter, not an additional expense. Those purchases were absent or privately paid. Forty copper remained in the relief chest, counted by the clerk and two household representatives. The missing thirty-eight had left the chest. They had not yet shown whose hand finally received it.

storm_compare_003.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_003.text: The steward said he used the thirty-eight as a temporary advance on a hauling cart. Market trade would earn it back before the next relief round. The cart stood behind his cousin's inn, fitted with an expensive axle. He produced a purchase agreement in his own name. Shen's jaw tightened. There was no shortage of actual payment evidence now. The remaining question was whether the council had authorized making damaged households lend to the steward's private business.

storm_compare_004.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_004.text: The council minutes approved immediate roof and grain protection grants, with no authority for private advances. The steward pointed to a sentence allowing urgent purchases. Its object was 'shelter material.' He argued that hauling capacity would help bring such material later. Jiang read the sentence aloud without finishing his argument for him. A cart could be useful to the village and still belong to a different account. Broad usefulness could not erase the owner named on the agreement.

storm_compare_005.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_005.text: Yue asked why the warning time had become after midnight in the published report. The steward said a late warning made the cart's purchase an emergency. Shen heard that as an admission of deliberate falsification. Jiang heard a statement worth copying exactly, then asked whether the steward had himself changed the time. He said yes. The clerk recorded the answer and his correction. The resulting evidence was stronger than a theory about blue ink or a haunted ledger.

storm_compare_006.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_006.text: He insisted the households would have received their money eventually. Yue thought of the carter's ankle and the roof reeds drying on the widow's floor. 'Eventually had a date in your plan,' she said. 'Did any of them know it?' The steward looked toward his pear, now wrinkled on the shelf. He had no answer. That silence did not prove every allegation. It made the already documented delay difficult to defend.

storm_compare_007.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_007.text: Shen wanted the account posted that afternoon. Yue wanted another interview with the absent scribe, whose copied wording had complicated the record. They could publish the confirmed payment discrepancy and steward's correction without naming the scribe as complicit. Elder Yun's reply reached them before lunch: preserve the mistaken phrase as a separate copying matter and send a formal request for explanation. Yue felt relieved, then embarrassed by how much she had wanted an elder to settle her uncertainty.

storm_compare_008.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_008.text: The warning repair drew from the ordinary road-maintenance allocation, separate from the disputed 180 copper and Yue's eighteen-copper copying pay. Its work order covered frame hardware, smith and leather repairs, supply stones and keeper checks. Jiang laid out the muffled handbell, split spare line and replacement lower signal frame. An enclosed charged stone would magnify a small permitted control trace. The bronze bell also had an ordinary hand lever. Yue could test a trigger after recovery; the stone would supply the repeated sound load.

storm_compare_009.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_009.text: The bell's smallest command was a quarter-unit pulse through the first established arm pair, with a half-unit delivery allowance and full discharge afterward. The second pair could be tested separately on a recovered day, never together merely to make the tone louder. Jiang checked the enclosed socket's stop before fitting its stone. Yue's eighteen usable units were a prior recovered reserve result. They were not an invitation to spend eighteen units at one sitting.

storm_compare_010.speaker: narrator
storm_compare_010.text: They could first compare the paid relay against a blank socket, rebuild the ordinary hand lever without qi, or audit how a warning moved from sender to receiver. All three methods would contribute to the replacement procedure. The village needed a reliable sound and a reliable meaning for that sound. Yue could begin with whichever part she understood best, while Jiang took responsibility for the remaining apparatus work and the clerk tracked the warning forms.

storm_test_choice.speaker: narrator
storm_test_choice.text: The new frame stood on a dry bench beside the wrapped handbell. A good tone would mean little if nobody knew who should act on it. A perfect instruction would mean little if its bell could not be heard. Jiang offered Yue one first responsibility: a supervised comparison, the ordinary lever, or the message procedure. The other tasks would proceed in parallel, then meet at a public drill.

choices.text: Compare the isolated trigger with a blank socket.
Rebuild and test the ordinary hand lever.
Trace the warning through named receivers.

storm_relay_001.speaker: narrator
storm_relay_001.text: The blank socket carried the same ceramic collar as the live socket but no charged stone. Yue checked the first-pair release through the grounded practice wick before Jiang connected either frame. Her recovered hand sensation was ordinary, and her last tested throughput remained unchanged. On the blank, the copper thread lit and the bell stayed silent. Their first useful result was a refusal: the control trace did not contain enough work to ring the frame by itself.

storm_relay_002.speaker: narrator
storm_relay_002.text: Jiang fitted the sleeved stone while the socket remained isolated. She wrote its starting charge beside the expected bell draw, then locked the cover. Yue delivered the permitted pulse and closed the route. The bell gave three clear strikes. The stone's measured decline included the trigger circuit and sound load. Yue's own expenditure included delivery and sampling losses. Two different budgets had performed one audible event, and neither could be made free by writing a single total.

storm_relay_003.speaker: narrator
storm_relay_003.text: On the next recovered morning, a loose thread in the control lead produced one clipped strike. Yue reached instinctively toward the cover before stopping at its guard. Jiang isolated the supply with the ordinary handle. They repaired the lead after the indicator went dark. The clipped sound mattered because households might interpret it as a different instruction. A frame that could fail halfway through its phrase needed an explicit fallback instead of a reassuring average.

storm_relay_004.speaker: narrator
storm_relay_004.text: They added a mechanical flag that dropped when the full three-strike cycle failed. The flag used the lever's ordinary movement, not another invisible reserve. A watcher at the lower shed would ring the handbell and carry a spoken warning if the flag fell. Yue liked the flag's blunt red cloth. It made the machine's uncertainty visible without asking a listener to judge the purity of a sound across wind and rain.

storm_relay_005.speaker: narrator
storm_relay_005.text: The second-pair trial waited for another recovered morning. Yue used its own previously permitted quarter-unit task and discharged fully before the first pair was considered again. The frame's output remained the same because its stone and mechanical stop determined the load. The test demonstrated independent interruption on an earned route. It opened no additional pair. Yue wrote that plain result beside the bell's attractive waveform and let the waveform remain attractive without enlarging the claim.

storm_relay_006.speaker: narrator
storm_relay_006.text: When the comparison ended, Jiang removed the practice stone and fitted the separately budgeted warning supply. The village keeper would own the charge checks. Yue gave him the blank result, the clipped-cycle example and the lever fallback. He asked whether the apprentice could remain nearby all season. She said the procedure had to work when she was home. The question sounded flattering until she recognized the old temptation to become a tool nobody could put down.

storm_lever_001.speaker: narrator
storm_lever_001.text: The ordinary hand lever pivoted on a bent iron pin. Yue set the unpowered frame on blocks while the keeper held its balance. They removed the pin, comparing it with a straight spare on a clean board. No spiritual sight was needed to see the crooked shadow. The smith would replace it; Yue could sand the wooden grip and check that the lever reached its stop without catching her sleeve.

storm_lever_002.speaker: narrator
storm_lever_002.text: The keeper showed her how the lever drove a small toothed wheel through three strikes. Its worn second tooth sometimes slipped. A louder swing merely made the third strike harder; it did not restore the missing middle sound. Yue had wanted to compensate with strength. She marked the tooth and sent the wheel to the smith with the pin. A failed part deserved repair, not a stronger apprentice repeatedly hiding its failure.

storm_lever_003.speaker: narrator
storm_lever_003.text: While the metal cooled, they inspected the handbell from the kitchen. Yue unwound the winter cord and found the clapper's leather joint cracked beneath it. Removing the muffling restored a sound, but the joint could break during a long warning. The leather worker replaced it and kept the damaged strip with its dated service tag. The handbell's history would remain visible even after the ordinary repair made it easy to forget.

storm_lever_004.speaker: narrator
storm_lever_004.text: At the public bench, three people of different heights tried the finished lever. The smallest could not reach its full travel while standing behind the marked guard. They lowered the grip by one peg and repeated the trial. Yue had tested it from her own stance and called it usable too soon. The keeper chalked the revised height on the wall. Ordinary access was a dimension of the apparatus, as real as the metal wheel's diameter.

storm_lever_005.speaker: narrator
storm_lever_005.text: A gust caught the shed door during the last trial. The door struck the lever's return and produced a false opening strike. Yue moved the frame inward, but Jiang required another whole-door swing before accepting the new position. It cleared with a finger's width to spare. They fitted a door hook as well. A warning device that rang because of its shelter would spend people's attention on weather before it communicated danger.

storm_lever_006.speaker: narrator
storm_lever_006.text: Jiang completed the separate powered-socket tests and showed Yue the flag that fell after an incomplete cycle. The ordinary lever could sound the same three strikes without any qi operator. The keeper tried it wearing thick rain gloves, then asked a second adult to repeat. Yue entered the repeated result in the maintenance book. Her fourth-stage cord hung beside the workbench, unnecessary to this task and still part of the worker who had done it.

storm_handover_001.speaker: narrator
storm_handover_001.text: The old instruction ended with the phrase 'inform the village.' Yue asked the clerk to replace it with actual actions people could test: receive the message, read back the affected area, send it to the bell keeper and check that a fallback receiver had answered. Shen said the new version looked longer. The clerk said its missing names had consumed an evening. Length on paper could purchase time when the weather stopped allowing questions.

storm_handover_002.speaker: narrator
storm_handover_002.text: The warning box's old mark recorded only that something arrived. They added a narrow receipt strip for the sender's retained copy, naming the receiving adult and the interval shown by the kitchen's lamp schedule. It would never provide a precise hour without a clock. Yue left space to write 'time uncertain.' The clerk preferred the empty line to be ruled out. After arguing, they printed those exact words so uncertainty could not look like a forgotten task.

storm_handover_003.speaker: narrator
storm_handover_003.text: The kitchen attendant practiced receiving a warning while stirring broth. She repeated the affected bridge correctly but forgot the refuge yard. Yue wanted her to start again from the beginning. Shen stopped the drill and asked her to finish tending the pot first. An instruction system could fail because it demanded two incompatible kinds of attention at once. They assigned a second receiver during meal work, rather than insisting an experienced cook should simply concentrate harder.

storm_handover_004.speaker: narrator
storm_handover_004.text: At the tower landing, the keeper rehearsed reporting a closed stair. This time the instruction required a spoken handover to the lower bell watcher and a returned acknowledgment. The runner used the route twice, once with the watcher deliberately absent. In that case he went to the kitchen for the ordinary handbell. Nobody called the absent watcher disobedient; the drill had arranged it. The missing person was a condition they wanted the procedure to survive.

storm_handover_005.speaker: narrator
storm_handover_005.text: Households disputed whether three strikes meant bridge closure or immediate shelter. Both customs had existed in different years. Yue showed them the conflicting old notices. The council agreed to retire the older phrase and post one short meaning beside the repaired refuge gate: protect exposed grain, keep off the lower bridge and gather in the high yard if home shelter was unsafe. Spoken warnings would repeat the same actions rather than inventing a new set.

storm_handover_006.speaker: narrator
storm_handover_006.text: When Jiang demonstrated the repaired frame, Yue watched the kitchen attendant instead of the bronze. She received the drill message, repeated its area and sent the runner. The lower watcher rang, then brought back a completed receipt strip. One household still misunderstood the grain instruction. They corrected the posted words and repeated the exercise. The system improved through another ordinary conversation, with the machine's successful tone supplying only one part of its success.

storm_warning_001.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_001.text: The public drill took place on the ninth morning. The village's lower warning shed had weather vanes, a bronze bell and an ordinary path bounded by rope rails. Jiang examined its ground bed and shut the storm-facing service box before anyone gathered. The replacement signal frame sat beneath the dry roof, mechanically apart from the old rod installation. Yue could help at its guarded bench. She had no task at the exposed vanes or the permanent storm conductor.

storm_warning_002.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_002.text: The council had announced the drill two days before, and the watcher called its beginning aloud. A practice message named the bridge and the grain sheds. Three strikes followed. Four households moved grain correctly; two sent children to investigate the sound. Yue heard the difference between a tone reaching an ear and a meaning reaching a household. The clerk marked the error on the drill sheet, then asked the children to demonstrate the new spoken instructions.

storm_warning_003.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_003.text: Cloud moved over the columns sooner than the road keeper expected. He stopped the drill and brought the distant carts below the checked lower turn. The storm compass's local vanes drifted beyond the morning blank. Jiang treated that as a reason to compare current weather observations, not a prediction of which roof would fail. The sky was dark enough to justify ending exposed work even if the compass had given them no reading.

storm_warning_004.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_004.text: The injured carter arrived with six grain sacks, his teenage loader driving while he sat with the splinted ankle raised. He refused to leave the wagon in the lower yard, fearing another delay would cost the buyer. The keeper barred the bridge anyway. Yue recognized the steward's earlier argument in another mouth: a future transaction offered as a reason to take today's unpriced risk. She helped move two sacks into the high shed while the unloading crew took the rest.

storm_warning_005.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_005.text: The warning frame sounded its full phrase once, powered by the counted village stone. The watcher then isolated it and used the handbell for nearby instructions. At the granary gate, the new planed bar lifted cleanly. The repaired passage mattered more in this rain than the argument that had requested it. Yue walked beneath the rope rail with a food crate, keeping both established arm routes quiet while wet boots and ordinary legs did their work.

storm_warning_006.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_006.text: Then the lower yard's side wall gave way. A beam had been weakened by the previous storm and hidden behind stacked sacks. The carter and teenage loader were trapped beyond the fallen panel on a strip of checked paving, the carter still seated with his splinted ankle supported. The grain shed roof remained stable, but runoff was rising along the narrow return. Jiang ordered the yard emptied and sent for the trained road crew. Yue could see the trapped pair. Two arm pairs could not lift a wet wall.

storm_warning_007.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_007.text: Jiang opened the rated rescue cabinet while the keeper inspected the ordinary escape paths from shelter. It held a shallow trolley, ropes with recent load tags and a portable barrier frame with four separately sleeved stones. The frame could shield a short withdrawal against falling fragments within its rated envelope. It could not halt a whole hillside or carry floodwater. The crew would abandon the trolley if its wheels or path failed the keeper's check.

storm_warning_008.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_008.text: The trapped pair had three useful possibilities. An intact raised strip led to the refuge gate; the trolley could support the carter's injured ankle along another checked passage; a loud signal could hold them in place until the road crew reached the sheltered side. Yue needed to choose her own first task while Jiang assigned the others. None required personal storm absorption. Each asked her to trust something less spectacular than a newly opened meridian.

storm_rescue_choice.speaker: narrator
storm_rescue_choice.text: The trained road crew reached sheltered staging as Jiang finished the cabinet check. Yue stood beneath the shed roof with the keeper beside her. The raised escape strip needed clear markers, the checked trolley passage needed hands at its ordinary brake, and the waiting pair needed a signal they could distinguish from the storm. Jiang would handle the rated shield. Yue could take one useful position while the crew worked from shelter and the shield drew from its own supply.

choices.text: Mark the raised ordinary escape strip.
Help the trolley's brake crew after the keeper's path check.
Repeat the handbell signal from the sheltered station.

storm_ground_001.speaker: narrator
storm_ground_001.text: The keeper checked the raised strip from its sheltered end before Yue moved. Its paving remained whole, and runoff passed beneath rather than over it. He fixed a rope marker at both ends while two adults watched the wall above. Yue carried the red flags along the ordinary route, stopping before the fallen panel. Jiang positioned the portable barrier between the shelter and the loose upper fragments. The barrier's four stones held its permitted field.

storm_ground_002.speaker: narrator
storm_ground_002.text: The loader mistook Yue's first flag for a command to jump. She lowered it and called the instruction in plain words: stay on the raised stone, move one person at a time, wait at the second mark. The loader repeated it back. Across the rain, understanding became something they could hear rather than assume. Yue planted the flag beside her boot instead of waving it again. A badly understood rescue signal could spend the intact path on the wrong movement.

storm_ground_003.speaker: narrator
storm_ground_003.text: The carter tried to rise on his damaged ankle and sank against the cart wheel. Yue stayed behind the marked boundary while the road crew approached from the high passage. They brought the shallow trolley with its ordinary brake and placed it on the keeper's second checked route. The ground strip would carry the loader; the trolley would carry the adult. One available escape did not have to serve two bodies with different limitations.

storm_ground_004.speaker: narrator
storm_ground_004.text: A small roof shard hit Jiang's barrier and fell on its outer side. The field indicator shortened as the protected withdrawal spent its stored charge. Yue watched the keeper, who watched the ordinary wall telltales. If the whole wall began moving, they would abandon the strip and pull back. It did not move during the pass. The loader reached the second flag with both feet on paving, breathing hard enough that Yue could hear him through the rain.

storm_ground_005.speaker: narrator
storm_ground_005.text: The crew rolled the carter along the other passage with two adults at the brake. Yue led the loader into the refuge yard and gave him a dry blanket. He wanted to return for the grain. She pointed to the barred gate and the crew's retreat. The grain could remain wet while the two of them stayed out of the yard. He cried angrily into the blanket, as if surviving had made his employer's loss his fault.

storm_ground_006.speaker: narrator
storm_ground_006.text: Under the granary roof, Jiang closed the barrier supply and counted its remaining charge before packing. The path had worked within the observed storm interval; it was closed again pending inspection. Yue removed the flags only after everyone was accounted for. Her hands shook from cold and ordinary effort. She did not call the shaking reflux, and Jiang did not dismiss it as courage. They warmed her hands before deciding whether any route sensation needed clinical review.

storm_trolley_001.speaker: narrator
storm_trolley_001.text: Yue took position at the trolley's rear beside a road worker who had hauled timber on the same wheels. The keeper inspected the sheltered passage, its drain and its turning clearance before giving them permission to advance. Jiang set the portable barrier between the route and loose upper fragments. Its four sleeved stones supplied the field. Yue's ordinary hands would work a brake on checked paving. Her established qi routes remained empty during the unfamiliar wet load.

storm_trolley_002.speaker: narrator
storm_trolley_002.text: The carter recognized her and tried to make a joke about needing another relief grant. Yue heard the fear underneath it. The road worker and a second adult shifted him onto the trolley while his splinted ankle stayed supported. Yue set the ordinary brake before they transferred his weight. The wheel chock held. A powerful-looking apprentice would have been less useful here than one who remembered which handle had to be fixed first.

storm_trolley_003.speaker: narrator
storm_trolley_003.text: At the first turn, one wheel met grit washed from the fallen wall. The trolley stopped short without lifting. Yue held the brake while the road worker cleared a hand's width of grit using a long scraper from shelter. They did not force the wheel over material the keeper had not checked. The indicator on Jiang's shield shortened during the pause. Delay had a protection cost, which she called aloud before permitting the next movement.

storm_trolley_004.speaker: narrator
storm_trolley_004.text: The loader wanted to climb onto the trolley beside the carter. Its load tag allowed the adult and supports, with no second rider on this narrow path. Yue directed the loader toward the raised strip, where the keeper's flags already marked a separate escape. He obeyed reluctantly. The rescue could carry both people by using two methods. It did not need to turn the rated cart into an unlimited promise just because rain made another wait unpleasant.

storm_trolley_005.speaker: narrator
storm_trolley_005.text: Two small shards struck the barrier's outer side as they crossed the last exposed stretch. Yue heard them and tightened her grip, but kept the brake movement slow enough for the wheels to hold. The crew brought the carter into the refuge yard and chocked the trolley before lifting him. Across the gate, the loader arrived under the red flags. Jiang ordered the whole route closed behind them instead of treating a successful withdrawal as permission for another trip.

storm_trolley_006.speaker: narrator
storm_trolley_006.text: Yue looked down at a blister beneath her thumb. She had made it with an ordinary wet handle, not a failed breakthrough. Jiang washed it, checked sensation and canceled the next day's trigger practice. The trolley needed its own wheel and brake inspection before reuse. The carter thanked Yue for the brake and the road worker for the lifting. Neither compliment changed the load tag or opened a third paired route in her arms.

storm_signal_001.speaker: narrator
storm_signal_001.text: The handbell hung beneath the dry shed roof beside its posted meaning. Yue rang the three-strike phrase and then shouted a specific instruction toward the trapped pair: stay on the marked paving, keep clear of the fallen panel, wait for the keeper's route signal. The loader raised one hand, but she could not know which words he understood. She asked him to repeat the last instruction, and heard 'wait for the keeper' come back.

storm_signal_002.speaker: narrator
storm_signal_002.text: The carter kept pointing toward the wagon's last sacks. Yue shouted that the wagon would remain while he left. It felt brutal to name his loss so plainly, yet a promise to recover everything might keep him beside the wall. Jiang installed the rated portable shield from the sheltered side, its four stones supporting only the short withdrawal zone. The keeper marked a raised strip for the loader while the road crew prepared a separate trolley passage.

storm_signal_003.speaker: narrator
storm_signal_003.text: A gust drowned Yue's next words. She stopped ringing instead of making louder meaningless sound and waited until the loader could see the keeper's flag. The trained road worker called from closer shelter, where the carter heard him clearly. Her station covered one part of the yard, not every ear in the rain. Yue marked that blind interval on the watcher card even while the crew began moving. A future drill would need another ordinary voice there.

storm_signal_004.speaker: narrator
storm_signal_004.text: The loader reached the raised strip first, moving after the keeper's signal. The carter tried to stand and failed on his splinted ankle. Yue called 'stay seated' to the nearer road worker, who repeated it beside the carter while the crew set the trolley brake. He remained seated for the transfer. Yue had helped by noticing a movement and sending a clear instruction through somebody close enough to be heard. The handbell waited at her station while words did that work.

storm_signal_005.speaker: narrator
storm_signal_005.text: A roof fragment struck Jiang's barrier, shortening its stored-charge indicator. Yue watched the carter's trolley cross the last protected stretch, then called 'crew in the refuge yard' to the watcher beside her. He repeated that limited report to the kitchen receiver. The keeper barred the damaged route again. Yue kept the bell quiet while the spoken report traveled. Anyone leaving a house to search for sacks would still meet a closed yard and a person who could explain its current danger.

storm_signal_006.speaker: narrator
storm_signal_006.text: At the granary bench, Yue wrapped the bell in a dry cloth with its clapper free. She could still hear its three strikes after the actual metal stopped. Jiang asked about finger pain and ordinary sensation before canceling tomorrow's trigger practice for everyone on the withdrawal. The sound did not leave Yue omniscient about the rescue. It left her with a station map that needed revision and two people she could count in the shelter.

storm_after_001.speaker: narrator
storm_after_001.text: The road crew accounted for every person in the yard before leaving its shelter. The carter's old fracture had not shifted according to the clinician's examination, though pain required another review. The loader had bruises and a torn sleeve. Yue needed warmth, food and a hand check after ordinary strain. The portable barrier had spent part of its counted supply. Jiang entered the actual used charge and sealed the remaining stones for their owner.

storm_after_002.speaker: narrator
storm_after_002.text: The fallen wall exposed an earlier repair patch behind the stacked sacks. The council's maintenance sheet listed the outer face as inspected, with no access to that inner patch. Shen wanted to call the old inspection worthless. The keeper said it had checked what it could reach. Their new report would preserve that limit and require moving stacks before another structural review. An inspection became dangerous when its small valid result was repeated as a complete guarantee.

storm_after_003.speaker: narrator
storm_after_003.text: Grain remained in the closed yard through the rain. Some sacks spoiled before the structural crew recovered them. The carter accused the keeper of choosing paper rules over livelihood. Yue could describe the checked escape, the shield's charge and the wall's uncertainty, but none restored his grain. The council arranged food support from a separate emergency allotment. They did not withhold it until he thanked the people who had kept him alive.

storm_after_004.speaker: narrator
storm_after_004.text: The loader said he had known about the wet patch for weeks. He had tried to tell the carter, who told him not to interrupt deliveries. Later he had assumed the adults knew. Jiang took his account privately with the clerk, then asked permission to include the maintenance fact without printing the boy's family address. His report would enter the structural inquiry. It would not become a public lesson about why a child should have been braver.

storm_after_005.speaker: narrator
storm_after_005.text: On the tenth morning, the lower warning frame remained isolated until Jiang rechecked its cover, ground bed and ordinary lever. The storm had brought mud to the shed's threshold but no water inside the locked socket. They replaced the wet route cards and added the signal blind interval to the watcher map. The new system had helped. Its observed mistakes still deserved repairs before the village called it reliable.

storm_after_006.speaker: narrator
storm_after_006.text: The steward appeared with a dry coat for the loader. The boy refused it, remembering the council's dishonest ledger. Yue took the coat to the shelter cupboard rather than making either person perform forgiveness. An act of ordinary help could remain available after its giver lost trust. It would not count as repayment of the thirty-eight copper. The clerk wrote the coat as an unsolicited shelter item, with no relief credit attached.

storm_after_007.speaker: narrator
storm_after_007.text: The cart seller answered Jiang's request with a duplicate invoice. Thirty-eight copper had been paid for the steward's cart, using the relief chest's numbered disbursement slip. The seller had delivered the cart and an installed axle exactly as contracted. There was no evidence he knew the money's source. His real sale explained the copper's destination. The private purchase remained unauthorized even if the seller had done honest work.

storm_after_008.speaker: narrator
storm_after_008.text: The seller offered to take the cart back for thirty-one copper, retaining seven for the fitted axle's removal and resale loss. The council's independent reviewer checked that price against two local offers. The steward could cover the remaining seven from his own purse or retain the cart and repay thirty-eight on an enforceable schedule. Yue asked the households which delay they could afford. Two roofs still had open holes. Waiting for his business to prosper would cost another wet week.

storm_after_009.speaker: narrator
storm_after_009.text: Mo Ran found Yue outside the archive with her hands tucked beneath her arms. She was furious at the steward and furious that his story had begun making sense. He had feared losing a private trade opportunity and called it village need. Understanding the fear did not authorize the transfer. Mo Ran listened until she finished, then asked whether she wanted tea or argument. She chose tea. Judgment would be easier after she was warm.

storm_after_010.speaker: narrator
storm_after_010.text: Shen brought a correction from the absent scribe. She had broadened the route phrase because the steward dictated that version during reconciliation. She admitted copying it without comparing the warning original. The clerk added her dated account to the evidence, leaving the contradiction visible. The steward disputed her memory of the dictation. The report could record that disagreement while relying on his own admitted time change and the independently matched cart invoice.

storm_after_011.speaker: narrator
storm_after_011.text: Elder Yun attended the preliminary review on the eleventh afternoon. She asked about the rope receipt, the thirty-eight-copper total and the wall's inspection limit before discussing any cultivation result. Yue showed her the separate recovered-route sheet, where the fourth stage remained unchanged. Yun nodded and returned to the ledger. A teacher could recognize Yue's earned skill without allowing it to distract from missing household money.

storm_after_012.speaker: narrator
storm_after_012.text: The public hearing was scheduled for the twelfth morning, the last day of Yue's copying task. Confirmed findings would be read aloud before disputed testimony. The household claimants could speak; the steward could answer; the independent reviewer would decide the recovery order under the council's own rules. Yue could present the transaction trace, describe the failed warning handovers, or help claimants check the proposed repayment list. Her choice would change what she had to face in the room.

storm_hearing_choice.speaker: narrator
storm_hearing_choice.text: The archive's long table had room for the original ledger, the copied receipts and a bowl of clean water. The clerk placed a chair beside each claimant's name. Yue had spent twelve days finding facts she could defend, and she still feared the moment when someone would call her ungrateful for reading them aloud. She chose one part of the hearing to carry, while Jiang and Shen presented the others.

choices.text: Read the copper's documented path to the private cart.
Explain each failed warning handover with its limits.
Check the household correction list beside the claimants.

storm_trace_001.speaker: narrator
storm_trace_001.text: Yue began with the counted chest, because its remaining forty copper could be checked without believing her. The clerk lifted the coins into four piles of ten. Then Yue read the net payments that totaled one hundred two and the three false support categories totaling thirty-eight. Together they accounted for the opening one hundred eighty. Nobody needed to infer an invisible fortune. The argument concerned a modest amount that had mattered enormously to people with broken roofs.

storm_trace_002.speaker: narrator
storm_trace_002.text: The widow's twenty-copper entry required its own explanation. Her receipt said twelve; her actual payment was ten. Eight had been redirected under the absent rope expense, and the two-copper levy had been pooled into the false fourteen-copper cover charge. The levy was not a thirty-ninth missing coin. The relief account had no authority for it. Yue asked the runner to confirm his retained note showing who instructed that deduction. The steward acknowledged the instruction was his.

storm_trace_003.speaker: narrator
storm_trace_003.text: Next came the cart invoice, its numbered disbursement slip and the seller's matching duplicate. The purchase did not become theft by magic when an apprentice read it aloud. Its funding violated the specific relief authorization, and the steward had made that violation harder to see with fictitious expense support. Yue stayed with those facts. She did not claim the seller knew, the scribe conspired or every previous council payment had been false.

storm_trace_004.speaker: narrator
storm_trace_004.text: The steward asked whether Yue thought a cart could never serve the village. She said it could, under an approved contract with the owner and price named. This purchase belonged to him. He tried to describe the delayed harvest trade, and she let him finish. His explanation had human urgency. It still did not turn eleven damaged roofs into willing lenders. The independent reviewer placed the cart agreement beside the council's shelter authorization, leaving both visible.

storm_trace_005.speaker: narrator
storm_trace_005.text: When Yue sat, her hands shook more than they had at the bell bench. She had wanted the numbers to protect her from anger. They had protected the scope of her claim, not the room's feelings. Shen poured her water while Jiang read the warning findings. Across the table, the widow mouthed her own name to make sure the clerk wrote it correctly. The hearing would succeed through several kinds of care, only one of them numerical.

storm_warning_hearing_001.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_hearing_001.text: Yue placed five cards along the table: delivered warning, council instruction, tower access, substitute sound and household action. She turned each card only after naming the evidence for it. The warning arrived before the final evening lamp issue. The runner met a closed stair. The split line and muffled handbell defeated assumed substitutes. None of those facts required the storm compass to reveal a person's intention. They described ordinary work handed off badly.

storm_warning_hearing_002.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_hearing_002.text: The keeper admitted closing the stair without personally checking the kitchen bell. The attendant admitted forgetting its winter cord. The runner admitted he returned without obtaining another named receiver. Yue included those admissions, then showed the old instruction that named none of the necessary fallback steps. The maintenance duties belonged to adults with different jobs. A missing procedure had made their assumptions compatible on paper while leaving the actual warning nowhere to go.

storm_warning_hearing_003.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_hearing_003.text: A council member proposed fining the kitchen attendant for every damaged roof. Jiang asked what portion of the loss the hearing could actually assign to her cord. Rainfall, building condition, the tower closure and household response all mattered. The hearing had no model capable of converting one forgotten cord into eleven roof prices. A duty correction and a disciplinary review could proceed under existing rules. An invented precise damage share would be another unsupported number.

storm_warning_hearing_004.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_hearing_004.text: Yue described the new drill's misunderstanding and the storm's signal blind interval along with its successes. Three strikes had reached the sheds; another ordinary voice had been needed behind the broken wall. The raised gate and separate trolley path helped the withdrawal. The barrier drew from its stones within its fragment rating. She kept the wall's incomplete earlier inspection in a separate structural finding. The warning procedure could improve without pretending it had repaired every building.

storm_warning_hearing_005.speaker: narrator
storm_warning_hearing_005.text: After the warning account, Shen presented the payment trace. The widow's two-copper levy appeared within the false fourteen-copper cover slip, not as extra money beyond the missing thirty-eight. The clerk read every net correction aloud. Yue listened with the other witnesses. Her own account had given the room a chain of actions to repair. The financial account gave it a debt to recover. Keeping both specific was harder than calling the whole storm a betrayal.

storm_claims_001.speaker: narrator
storm_claims_001.text: The widow sat beside Yue while the clerk laid out four corrected household entries. Their net shortfalls were ten, eight, eight and twelve copper, totaling thirty-eight. Other grants had reached their recipients as recorded. Yue checked the names against each claimant rather than letting an accurate sum make a misspelled name acceptable. The carter wanted a new grain claim heard immediately. That later loss belonged to a separate emergency assessment, which the clerk scheduled for the next day.

storm_claims_002.speaker: narrator
storm_claims_002.text: The widow's nominal twelve-copper receipt had concealed a two-copper levy, leaving ten actually paid against a twenty-copper entry. Eight of the missing ten had been coded as rope. The levy formed part of the false fourteen-copper cover charge. Yue drew the ten as eight and two on a slate, then rubbed out the larger total and rebuilt it with the widow watching. A correct account had to be understandable to the person whose payment it described.

storm_claims_003.speaker: narrator
storm_claims_003.text: Two households shared the privately bought cover. Its full fourteen-copper receipt had been copied as a relief-funded expense, though neither received reimbursement. Their actual approved grant shortfalls did not divide according to the cloth's price. The false expense categories described how the steward disguised the diversion; the household correction list described who was owed money. Yue kept those lists apart on the table so a repair seller would not accidentally receive the grant twice.

storm_claims_004.speaker: narrator
storm_claims_004.text: The runner's two-copper levy note was read beside the steward's admission that he ordered it. The deduction was unauthorized, included in the thirty-eight diverted copper and owed back through the widow's ten-copper correction. Yue watched the widow nod. A council member suggested accepting her old receipt as proof of full payment. The independent reviewer rejected that because the recipient, collector's note and corrected transaction trace established the smaller actual amount.

storm_claims_005.speaker: narrator
storm_claims_005.text: By the time Jiang finished the warning account, each claimant had checked the net sum beside their name. Agreement on a repayment list did not require them to endorse the steward's explanation or forgive the delay. Yue asked the clerk to leave room for a later complaint if the payment failed to arrive. The line looked small, but the widow tapped it with one fingernail. A new promise needed a place where its failure could be written.

storm_settle_001.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_001.text: The independent reviewer ordered recovery of thirty-eight copper to the relief chest and payment of the four corrected grants. The steward chose to return the cart. The seller would refund thirty-one after inspecting its unused body and fitted axle; the steward would provide seven from his own purse. The order named dates and a receiving clerk. It did not credit an offered coat, a helpful speech or the value of the cart's imagined future journeys.

storm_settle_002.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_002.text: The steward asked to keep signing village expense summaries. The council suspended that duty pending its separate disciplinary review. Two other adults would authorize relief disbursement, with the clerk keeping a copy each recipient could read. Yue disliked the word 'pending' after so many delays, but the review had specific dates and authority outside her commission. Her findings justified the immediate money order. They did not confer a permanent power to choose the village's officers.

storm_settle_003.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_003.text: The cart returned to the seller that afternoon. He checked the axle number against his invoice and counted thirty-one copper into the clerk's receiving tray. The steward added seven under the same recovery entry. Shen copied the axle number and refund signature while two witnesses counted the tray again. The copper had an actual path back, and the receiving entry could be checked against both the signed refund and the counted balance.

storm_settle_004.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_004.text: At the archive counter, the four households received ten, eight, eight and twelve copper. Each counted the coins before signing a new receipt. The widow asked to keep the old twelve-copper paper as well. The clerk marked it superseded rather than destroying it. The chest now held forty copper after total legitimate payments of one hundred forty. The ending balance matched the starting one hundred eighty without hiding the intervening diversion.

storm_settle_005.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_005.text: Yue's twelve-day copying wages were paid from the independent road fund as agreed. She set the eighteen copper apart from the relief recipients' trays. The work had helped them, and it had been work. She could buy food without calling the grant money hers, and they could judge the report without owing her gratitude. Shen asked whether she would miss the archive. She looked at her cramped fingers and said she might miss its window.

storm_settle_006.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_006.text: The scribe's disputed account remained attached to the hearing record. Its route wording had been corrected against the warning original, while the disagreement about dictation stayed attributed to both speakers. No evidence justified a wider claim that every scribe's entry was corrupt. Elder Yun signed the comparison note and declined to issue a spiritual judgment of guilt. Her seal confirmed the documents she had compared. It would not replace the council's disciplinary process.

storm_settle_007.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_007.text: The warning shed received a weekly ordinary check and a monthly isolated powered comparison by its qualified keeper. The kitchen handbell's clapper stayed free. The refuge gate's swollen bar went on the carpenter's seasonal list. The damaged wall and grain yard remained closed until structural repairs and independent checks. A clearer warning could help people avoid danger; it could not turn a warning sound into proof that the destination building was safe.

storm_settle_008.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_008.text: Three recovered days after the hearing, Yue's hand sensation returned to baseline. Jiang supervised a short first-pair task with measured delivery, known apparatus draw and full discharge. The second pair waited until another recovered day and was checked separately. Both remained within their established allowances. Yue's fourth-stage record stood. Her control had improved through ordinary practice and interruption, while the four-pair examination still required routes and trials she had not performed.

storm_settle_009.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_009.text: Duan Zhi's letter reached the workshop on the fifth recovered morning. Salt Lantern Valley wanted ordinary cistern and sluice workers as falling lake water exposed an old boundary channel. Nineteen restored household claims remained in the registry, yet the water schedule still treated erased names as absent. Jiang said the storm report's certified extract might help them compare purchases. Its documented financial findings could travel only as far as the transactions it actually established.

storm_settle_010.speaker: narrator
storm_settle_010.text: Before choosing the next road, Yue could stay briefly to help publish the corrected ledger, take a paid workshop turn maintaining the portable bell frame, or go home with her wages and let the keepers own the procedure. Each led toward the valley invitation after three weeks. The village's repairs would continue without her. She had learned enough to contribute another useful task, and enough to let a finished one become somebody else's ordinary responsibility.

storm_final_choice.speaker: narrator
storm_final_choice.text: The corrected receipts dried beneath their light paper weights. Outside, the warning bell's keeper practiced with its ordinary lever. Yue could help make the financial account readable in public, improve the workshop maintenance notes, or return to the west kiln before the valley commission began. She still wanted four paired routes. These choices would determine the work she did while remaining a practitioner with two, rather than pretending the next stage had arrived unnoticed.

choices.text: Help publish the corrected storm ledger and its evidence limits.
Take the paid portable-bell workshop turn.
Go home with the corrected account and prepare for the valley road.

storm_public_001.speaker: narrator
storm_public_001.text: The public posting used two pages. One traced the thirty-eight-copper diversion and actual repayment. The other showed the failed warning handovers and the new procedure. Yue read them at the grain counter on three different mornings, because not everyone could leave work for the hearing. The third reading drew fewer listeners. The ledger was becoming ordinary village knowledge rather than a performance centered on the apprentice who had helped correct it.

storm_public_002.speaker: narrator
storm_public_002.text: A man asked whether the new notice proved the steward had caused the storm. Yue pointed to the weather observations and shook her head. He had diverted relief money and changed a reported time. The storm had its own conditions. The wall had its own repair failure. Keeping those statements separate did not soften the offense; it prevented the notice from creating a new superstition powerful enough to blame every future rain on a disliked neighbor.

storm_public_003.speaker: narrator
storm_public_003.text: The widow checked her name on the posting and found it correct. Then she asked why a paragraph listed the carter's broken ankle without his trade schedule. Yue asked the carter which public financial fields he approved. With his written agreement, she added the income consequence while keeping clinical details private. A fact could be true and still be poorly chosen for a public wall. The certified underlying record remained intact, with recipients able to inspect the fuller entries through the clerk.

storm_public_004.speaker: narrator
storm_public_004.text: Jiang paid Yue for the three publication mornings from the road fund's education allowance. Shen helped bind a certified extract for Salt Lantern Valley. It contained the purchase trace, the correction method and the warning handover diagram. It named no valley debtor and authorized no accusation elsewhere. Yue would carry a worked example of comparing records. The people at the next commission would still deserve questions about their own documents.

storm_public_005.speaker: narrator
storm_public_005.text: Three weeks after the hearing, Yue packed the extract beside her repaired tablet. The fourth-stage cord rested on her sleeve, faded by wet work and ordinary washing. She left the public originals with the clerk and said goodbye to the bell keeper, who no longer needed her at the lever. Along the valley road, a low line of lantern posts stood beyond the reeds. A new account waited there, with its own water and its own missing names.

storm_end_public.speaker: narrator
storm_end_public.text: At the valley turn, Yue opened the extract only to check its wax tie. The hearing's result remained specific: thirty-eight copper recovered, four grants corrected, warning duties repaired and disputed testimony retained. That was enough to be useful without becoming a universal verdict. Duan Zhi's receiving address lay on the outer cover. She carried the account toward it, ready to discover where the next village's arithmetic and ordinary lives disagreed.
storm_end_public.ending: An Account That Can Be Read

storm_workshop_001.speaker: narrator
storm_workshop_001.text: Yue accepted six short workshop days, with recovery mornings between the two qualified trigger comparisons. Most of the work involved ordinary screws, leather joints and legible service tags. The portable bell's bronze surface acquired fingerprints no polishing schedule could prevent. She learned to like those marks. An apparatus that lived among people needed a maintenance book, not the appearance of remaining forever untouched since its celebrated first success.

storm_workshop_002.speaker: narrator
storm_workshop_002.text: The keeper tried the service procedure with Yue watching silently. He checked the free clapper, lever travel, supply cover and incomplete-cycle flag. He forgot to record the stone's remaining charge until the last line. Yue moved that line higher in the form after discussing his usual working order. The form should guide a tired keeper toward the important check. A blank field at the bottom could not perform the work merely by existing.

storm_workshop_003.speaker: narrator
storm_workshop_003.text: The workshop built a second portable frame for a dated loan to Salt Lantern Valley's dry-season commission. Its ordinary lever could supply neutral time signals, and its enclosed powered cycle used a separately rated stone under a qualified keeper. Jiang removed the storm-specific meaning from its sign plate. A water-maintenance crew needed a scheduled work signal, not a bell that told households to shelter whenever someone tested a sluice. Yue copied both procedures, including the frame's return date, without merging their sounds into one universal command.

storm_workshop_004.speaker: narrator
storm_workshop_004.text: On the fifth worked day, a control lead failed at its leather strain relief. Yue had just delivered the permitted first-pair task and discharged; Jiang isolated the socket before inspection. The lead's repair was logged as apparatus maintenance. It did not become evidence that Yue's second pair had failed, nor a reason to repeat both routes under fatigue. On the sixth worked day, after recovery, the restored frame passed its separate ordinary and qualified tests within the agreed workshop term.

storm_workshop_005.speaker: narrator
storm_workshop_005.text: Three weeks after the hearing, Yue left with the portable frame on a checked cart and Jiang's signed service pack. The frame and supplied stones remained workshop property under the dated valley loan, with their actual charge and handling limits listed. Her wages paid for food; they were not spent to feed the bell's stone. At the first lantern post, she stopped the cart with its ordinary brake. The next job would begin with checking where its sound could be heard.

storm_end_workshop.speaker: narrator
storm_end_workshop.text: The bell stayed covered along the valley road, its clapper secured for travel rather than forgotten beneath winter cord. Yue carried the service pack in a dry pocket and left the original storm ledger at the archive. The frame could mark public working intervals once the local crew chose their meaning. It could not decide who deserved water. That decision awaited gauges, names and a village whose story she had not yet heard.

storm_home_001.speaker: narrator
storm_home_001.text: At the west kiln, Yue put her wages on the familiar shelf and gave her mother the corrected public account. Her mother read the payment list before asking about the rescue. She had expected a tale of lightning mastered through cultivation. Yue described the keeper's paving check, the trolley brake and a shield supplied by its stones. Her mother nodded, then asked whether the loader had eaten. The ordinary question reached the part Yue had been missing.

storm_home_002.speaker: narrator
storm_home_002.text: They repaired the flour shelf on an afternoon when the kiln was cool. Yue used a wooden wedge beneath its short leg and checked it with the jar filled. Her mother brought out an inland grain-house receipt tucked behind the old warning notice. It included a seasonal water surcharge for Salt Lantern Valley. The date matched an interval when the public supply schedule claimed that grain-house had drawn nothing. A receipt from another place offered a question, not another guilty steward.

storm_home_003.speaker: narrator
storm_home_003.text: Yue copied the surcharge, seller's name and printed interval, then returned the receipt to its owner. She wrote to Duan Zhi asking whether grain-house water purchases would fall within the valley maintenance inquiry. His reply arrived with the commission details and a request for a witnessed copy. He did not promise a finding before seeing the schedule. Yue recognized the value of that unanswered space more readily than she had at the archive's first table.

storm_home_004.speaker: narrator
storm_home_004.text: During the three weeks before departure, she practiced only recovered tasks through her two established arm pairs. Some mornings ordinary kiln work left no useful reserve for a separate comparison, and she wrote that plainly. Her mother began asking about sleep before asking about qi. The fourth-stage cord stayed beside the repaired tablet at supper. It could mark an earned result without becoming a demand that every household hour prove the next one.

storm_home_005.speaker: narrator
storm_home_005.text: Yue packed the witnessed receipt copy after breakfast on the valley departure day. The original remained beneath her mother's flour shelf, now level under its usual load. She took the approved storm extract as well, because comparing one known correction might help ask better questions elsewhere. Beyond the west road, lantern posts leaned toward a receding line of water. She would reach them with an ordinary fare and an account that had room for disagreement.

storm_end_home.speaker: narrator
storm_end_home.text: Her mother stood at the kiln gate until Yue reached the turn. The inland receipt carried a date, an amount and a vendor's claim about water. It carried no verdict about the valley. Yue touched the dry cover of her tablet and continued toward Duan Zhi's address. The storm had taught her to follow a payment far enough to answer its question. The next road would teach her which question this payment actually asked.
storm_end_home.ending: A Receipt Beneath the Flour Shelf
